from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union


def truncate_text(text: str, max_chars: int, ellipsis: str = "...") -> str:
    """
    Shorten `text` for previews and teasers without cutting words in half.

    The text is first cleaned with normalize_whitespace(). If the cleaned text has
    at most `max_chars` characters it is returned as is. Otherwise the result is the
    longest run of whole leading words (joined by single spaces) such that the
    words plus `ellipsis` fit in max_chars characters, followed by `ellipsis`. If
    not even the first word fits, the first word is hard-cut so that the result is
    exactly max_chars characters long. Raises ValueError if
    max_chars <= len(ellipsis).

    Examples:
        truncate_text("The quick brown fox jumps", 15) == "The quick..."
        truncate_text("Short text", 50) == "Short text"
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union


def top_words(text: str, k: int, stopwords: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
    """
    Return the `k` most frequent words of `text` as (word, count) pairs, most
    frequent first. Feeds the "top terms" panel of the article analytics page.

    Words come from tokenize_words(). Words listed in `stopwords` (compared
    case-insensitively) are ignored, and so are tokens made only of digits. If fewer
    than k distinct words remain, all of them are returned. Raises ValueError if
    k < 0.

    Examples:
        top_words("b a b c b a", 2) == [("b", 3), ("a", 2)]
        top_words("Data, data and more DATA", 1, stopwords=["and"]) == [("data", 3)]
    """

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union


def closest_match(word: str, vocabulary: Iterable[str], max_distance: int = 2) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Suggest the vocabulary entry closest to `word` (the "did you mean ...?" hint
    under the search box).

    Distances are computed with edit_distance() on the lowercased strings. Returns
    the entry with the smallest distance, provided that distance is <=
    max_distance; returns None when nothing is close enough or the vocabulary is
    empty. When several entries share the smallest distance, the one that appears
    first in `vocabulary` wins. The entry is returned with its original spelling.
    Raises ValueError if max_distance is negative.

    Examples:
        closest_match("pyhton", ["python", "pandas"]) == "python"
        closest_match("zzz", ["python"]) is None
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union


def justify_text(text: str, width: int) -> List[str]:
    """
    Fully justify `text` to a fixed column width for plain-text newsletters.

    Lines are produced with wrap_text(text, width). Every line except the last one
    is then stretched to exactly `width` characters by widening the gaps between
    its words: the extra spaces are spread as evenly as possible, and when they do
    not divide evenly the leftmost gaps get one more space than the others.
    The last line is left-aligned (single spaces between words), and so is any
    line that holds a single word. A line already longer than width (a single
    over-long word) is left as it is. Raises ValueError if width < 1.

    Example:
        justify_text("This is an example of text justification.", 16)[:2]
            == ["This    is    an", "example  of text"]
    """

def slugify(text: str, max_length: Optional[int] = None) -> str:
    """
    Build a URL slug from a title.

    The text is split into words with tokenize_words(). Each word is reduced to
    ASCII by stripping diacritics (Unicode NFKD decomposition, then dropping
    non-ASCII characters), after which any remaining character other than a-z and
    0-9 is removed; words that end up empty are discarded. The remaining words are
    joined with "-", so the slug only contains a-z, 0-9 and "-".

    If `max_length` is given, the slug is shortened to at most max_length
    characters and never ends with "-". Raises ValueError if max_length is given
    and is < 1.

    Examples:
        slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world"
        slugify("Crème Brûlée Recipes") == "creme-brulee-recipes"
        slugify("50% off: Summer Sale") == "50-off-summer-sale"

import re
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple

_HEADING = re.compile(r" {0,3}(#{1,6})(?:[ \t]+(.*?))?[ \t]*")
_FENCE = re.compile(r" {0,3}(```|~~~)")
_CLOSING = re.compile(r"(?:^|[ \t]+)#+$")


def extract_headings(markdown: str) -> List[Tuple[int, str]]:
    headings: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
    fence: Optional[str] = None
    for line in markdown.splitlines():
        fence_match = _FENCE.match(line)
        if fence_match:
            if fence is None:
                fence = fence_match.group(1)
            elif fence == fence_match.group(1):
                fence = None
            continue
        if fence is not None:
            continue
        match = _HEADING.fullmatch(line)
        if match:
            title = _CLOSING.sub("", match.group(2) or "").strip()
            headings.append((len(match.group(1)), title))
    return headings

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any

_PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(r"\{\{\s*([^{}]*?)\s*\}\}")
_FILTERS = (("upper", str.upper), ("lower", str.lower), ("title", str.title), ("trim", str.strip))


def _lookup(context: Mapping, path: str) -> Any:
    value: Any = context
    for part in path.split("."):
        if not isinstance(value, Mapping) or part not in value:
            raise KeyError(path)
        value = value[part]
    return value


def render_template(template: str, context: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
    filters = dict(_FILTERS)

    def replace(match):
        name, *filter_names = [piece.strip() for piece in match.group(1).split("|")]
        value = _lookup(context, name)
        text = "" if value is None else str(value)
        for filter_name in filter_names:
            if filter_name not in filters:
                raise ValueError(f"unknown filter: {filter_name}")
            text = filters[filter_name](text)
        return text

from typing import Dict, List

from textkit.extract_headings import extract_headings
from textkit.slugify import slugify


def table_of_contents(markdown: str, max_level: int = 3) -> str:
    if not 1 <= max_level <= 6:
        raise ValueError("max_level must be between 1 and 6")
    seen: Dict[str, int] = {}
    entries = []
    for level, title in extract_headings(markdown):
        base = slugify(title)
        if not base:
            continue
        count = seen.get(base, 0)
        seen[base] = count + 1
        anchor = base if count == 0 else f"{base}-{count}"
        if level <= max_level:
            entries.append((level, title, anchor))
    if not entries:
        return ""
    top = min(level for level, _, _ in entries)
    lines: List[str] = []
    for level, title, anchor in entries:
        lines.append(f"{'  ' * (level - top)}- [{title}](#{anchor})")
    return "\n".join(lines)

from typing import List


def split_csv_line(line: str, delimiter: str = ",") -> List[str]:
    if len(delimiter) != 1 or delimiter == '"':
        raise ValueError("delimiter must be a single character other than a double quote")
    fields: List[str] = []
    pos, end = 0, len(line)
    while True:
        probe = pos
        while probe < end and line[probe] == " " and delimiter != " ":
            probe += 1
        if probe < end and line[probe] == '"':
            probe += 1
            chars = []
            while True:
                if probe >= end:
                    raise ValueError("unterminated quoted field")
                if line[probe] == '"':
                    if probe + 1 < end and line[probe + 1] == '"':
                        chars.append('"')
                        probe += 2
                        continue
                    probe += 1
                    break
                chars.append(line[probe])
                probe += 1
            if probe < end and line[probe] != delimiter:
                raise ValueError("unexpected text after closing quote")
            fields.append("".join(chars))
        else:
            probe = line.find(delimiter, pos)
            if probe == -1:
                probe = end
            fields.append(line[pos:probe])
        if probe >= end:
            return fields
        pos = probe + 1

def count_syllables(word: str) -> int:
    """
    Estimate the number of syllables in an English word (heuristic used by the
    readability score).

    The word is lowercased and every character other than a-z is removed. Then:
      1. Count the groups of consecutive vowels, where vowels are a, e, i, o, u, y.
      2. Silent e: if the word ends in "e" and there is more than one vowel group,

      3. The result is never below 1 for a word that has at least one letter.
    A word with no letters a-z at all returns 0.

def split_sentences(text: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Split prose into sentences.

    The text is first cleaned with normalize_whitespace() and then split into
    space-separated words. A word ends a sentence when:
      * it ends with a terminator run of ".", "!" or "?" (e.g. "...", "?!"),
        optionally followed by closing quotes or brackets (" ' ) ]), and
      * the next word starts with an uppercase letter, a digit, or an opening
        quote/bracket (" ' ( [).

    case-sensitive match): Mr. Mrs. Ms. Dr. Prof. St. vs. e.g. i.e.
    Whatever follows the last boundary is the final sentence. Each sentence is
    its words joined by single spaces; sentences are returned in order, and empty
    input gives [].

    Examples:
        split_sentences("Hello there. How are you? Fine!") == ["Hello there.", "How are you?", "Fine!"]

from typing import List, Sequence, Tuple

from textkit.similarity import similarity


def rank_matches(query: str, candidates: Sequence[str], limit: int = 5, min_score: float = 0.0) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
    """
    Rank `candidates` by how closely they match `query` and return the best ones
    as (candidate, score) pairs, best score first. Used by the tag picker.

    The score of a candidate is similarity(query, candidate). Candidates scoring
    below `min_score` are dropped, then at most `limit` pairs are returned.
    Duplicate candidate strings are only ranked once. `candidates` is not modified.
    Raises ValueError if limit < 0.

    Example:
        rank_matches("python", ["java", "python", "pythons"], limit=2)
            == [("python", 1.0), ("pythons", 0.86)]
    """
    if limit < 0:
        raise ValueError("limit must be >= 0")

    seen: set[str] = set()
    scored: List[Tuple[str, float]] = []
    for cand in candidates:
        if cand in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(cand)
        score = similarity(query, cand)
        if score >= min_score:
            scored.append((cand, score))

    scored.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[1], reverse=True)
    return scored[:limit]
"},"messages":[]}

def split_identifier(name: str) -> List[str]:

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union


def edit_distance(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """
    Return the edit distance between `a` and `b`: the minimum number of
    single-character edits needed to turn `a` into `b`.

    Inserting, deleting or substituting one character each cost 1. The comparison
    is case-sensitive, and the distance is symmetric:
    edit_distance(a, b) == edit_distance(b, a). Used by search suggestions for
    typo tolerance.

    Examples:
        edit_distance("kitten", "sitting") == 3
        edit_distance("", "abc") == 3
    """
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    prev = list(range(m + 1))
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        curr = [i] + [0] * m
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            cost = 0 if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] else 1
            curr[j] = min(
                prev[j] + 1,      # delete
                curr[j - 1] + 1,  # insert
                prev[j - 1] + cost,  # substitute
            )
        prev = curr
    return prev[m]

from typing import List, Sequence, Tuple

from textkit.similarity import similarity


def rank_matches(query: str, candidates: Sequence[str], limit: int = 5, min_score: float = 0.0) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
    """
    Rank `candidates` by how closely they match `query` and return the best ones
    as (candidate, score) pairs, best score first. Used by the tag picker.

    The score of a candidate is similarity(query, candidate). Candidates scoring
    below `min_score` are dropped, then at most `limit` pairs are returned.
    Duplicate candidate strings are only ranked once. `candidates` is not modified.
    Raises ValueError if limit < 0.

    Example:
        rank_matches("python", ["java", "python", "pythons"], limit=2)
            == [("python", 1.0), ("pythons", 0.86)]
    """
    if limit < 0:
        raise ValueError("limit must be >= 0")

    seen: set = set()
    scored: List[Tuple[str, float]] = []
    for cand in candidates:
        if cand in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(cand)
        score = similarity(query, cand)
        if score >= min_score:
            scored.append((cand, score))

    scored.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[1], reverse=True)
    return scored[:limit]
"}},"messages":[]}

def truncate_text(text: str, max_chars: int, ellipsis: str = "...") -> str:

    best_run = ""

        else:

import re

from textkit.tokenize_words import _TOKEN_RE

_MINOR_WORDS = {"a", "an", "for", "in", "of", "on", "the", "to"}


def make_acronym(phrase: str) -> str:
    """
    Build an acronym from the first character of each word of `phrase`.

    Words come from tokenize_words(), so hyphenated parts count as separate words
    ("self-contained" contributes "SC"). Letters are upper-cased; a word that starts
    with a digit contributes that digit. Returns "" when the phrase has no words.

    House style keeps minor words visible but in lower case: when one of a, an,
    for, in, of, on, the, to appears anywhere except as the first word, its letter
    is kept lowercase.

    Examples:
        make_acronym("Portable Network Graphics") == "PNG"
        make_acronym("self-contained underwater breathing apparatus") == "SCUBA"
        make_acronym("Department of Defense") == "DoD"
        make_acronym("The Lord of the Rings") == "TLotR"
    """
    text = phrase.replace("\u2019", "'")
    tokens = _TOKEN_RE.findall(text)

    letters: list[str] = []
    for index, token in enumerate(tokens):
        first = token[0]
        if index > 0 and first.lower() in _MINOR_WORDS:
            letters.append(first.lower())
        else:
            letters.append(first.upper())
    return "".join(letters)

from .tokenize_words import tokenize_words


def slugify(text: str, max_length: Optional[int] = None) -> str:
    """
    Build a URL slug from a title.

    The text is split into words with tokenize_words(). Each word is reduced to
    ASCII by stripping diacritics (Unicode NFKD decomposition, then dropping
    non-ASCII characters), after which any remaining character other than a-z and
    0-9 is removed; words that end up empty are discarded. The remaining words are
    joined with "-", so the slug only contains a-z, 0-9 and "-".

    If `max_length` is given, the slug is shortened to at most max_length
    characters and never ends with "-". Raises ValueError if max_length is given
    and is < 1.

    Examples:
        slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world"
        slugify("Crème Brûlée Recipes") == "creme-brulee-recipes"
        slugify("50% off: Summer Sale") == "50-off-summer-sale"
    """
    if max_length is not None and max_length < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_length must be >= 1")

    def normalize_word(word: str) -> str:
        # NFKD decomposition to separate base characters from diacritics
        normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", word)
        # Keep only ASCII characters
        ascii_only = "".join(c for c in normalized if ord(c) < 128)
        # Keep only a-z and 0-9
        return "".join(c for c in ascii_only if c.isalnum())

    normalized_words = []
    for token in tokens:
        normalized = normalize_word(token)
        if normalized:
            normalized_words.append(normalized)

    # Join with hyphens
    slug = "-".join(normalized_words)

    # Handle max_length
    if max_length is not None:
        if len(slug) <= max_length:
            return slug

        # Need to shorten
        result_words = []
        current_length = 0

        for word in normalized_words:
            # Calculate length if we add this word
            if result_words:
                new_length = current_length + 1 + len(word)  # +1 for hyphen
            else:

                current_length = new_length

                if not result_words:

                    result_words.append(word[:max_length])
                # Stop adding more words

import unicodedata
from typing import Optional

from .tokenize_words import tokenize_words


def slugify(text: str, max_length: Optional[int] = None) -> str:
    """
    Build a URL slug from a title.

    The text is split into words with tokenize_words(). Each word is reduced to
    ASCII by stripping diacritics (Unicode NFKD decomposition, then dropping
    non-ASCII characters), after which any remaining character other than a-z and
    0-9 is removed; words that end up empty are discarded. The remaining words are
    joined with "-", so the slug only contains a-z, 0-9 and "-".

    If `max_length` is given, the slug is shortened to at most max_length
    characters and never ends with "-". Raises ValueError if max_length is given
    and is < 1.

    Examples:
        slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world"
        slugify("Crème Brûlée Recipes") == "creme-brulee-recipes"
        slugify("50% off: Summer Sale") == "50-off-summer-sale"
    """
    if max_length is not None and max_length < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_length must be >= 1")

    def normalize_word(word: str) -> str:
        # NFKD decomposition to separate base characters from diacritics
        normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", word)
        # Keep only ASCII characters
        ascii_only = "".join(c for c in normalized if ord(c) < 128)
        # Keep only a-z and 0-9
        return "".join(c for c in ascii_only if c.isalnum())

    # Tokenize and normalize words
    tokens = tokenize_words(text)
    normalized_words = []
    for token in tokens:
        normalized = normalize_word(token)
        if normalized:
            normalized_words.append(normalized)

    # Join with hyphens
    slug = "-".join(normalized_words)

    # Handle max_length
    if max_length is not None:
        if len(slug) <= max_length:
            return slug

        # Need to shorten
        result_words = []
        current_length = 0

        for word in normalized_words:
            # Calculate length if we add this word
            if result_words:
                new_length = current_length + 1 + len(word)  # +1 for hyphen
            else:
                new_length = len(word)

            if new_length <= max_length:
                result_words.append(word)
                current_length = new_length
            else:
                # Can't fit this word entirely
                if not result_words:
                    # First word alone is too long, truncate it
                    result_words.append(word[:max_length])
                # Stop adding more words
                break

        slug = "-".join(result_words)

    return slug

from typing import List

from textkit.normalize_whitespace import normalize_whitespace

_ABBREVIATIONS: frozenset = frozenset({
    "Mr.", "Mrs.", "Ms.", "Dr.", "Prof.", "St.", "vs.", "e.g.", "i.e.",
})

_TERMINATORS: frozenset = frozenset(".!?")

_CLOSERS: frozenset = frozenset("'\")]")

_OPENERS: frozenset = frozenset("'\"([")


def _ends_with_terminator(word: str) -> bool:
    """Check if word ends with a terminator run, optionally followed by closers."""
    stripped = word.rstrip("'\")]")
    if not stripped:
        return False
    return stripped[-1] in _TERMINATORS


def _next_word_starts_sentence(next_word: str) -> bool:
    """Check if the next word starts with uppercase, digit, or opening quote/bracket."""
    if not next_word:
        return False
    c = next_word[0]
    return c.isupper() or c.isdigit() or c in _OPENERS


def split_sentences(text: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Split prose into sentences.

    The text is first cleaned with normalize_whitespace() and then split into
    space-separated words. A word ends a sentence when:
      * it ends with a terminator run of ".", "!" or "?" (e.g. "...", "?!"),
        optionally followed by closing quotes or brackets (" ' ) ]), and
      * the next word starts with an uppercase letter, a digit, or an opening
        quote/bracket (" ' ( [).
    Words that are one of these abbreviations never end a sentence (exact,
    case-sensitive match): Mr. Mrs. Ms. Dr. Prof. St. vs. e.g. i.e.
    Whatever follows the last boundary is the final sentence. Each sentence is
    its words joined by single spaces; sentences are returned in order, and empty
    input gives [].

    Examples:
        split_sentences("Hello there. How are you? Fine!") == ["Hello there.", "How are you?", "Fine!"]
        split_sentences("Ask Dr. Smith. He knows.") == ["Ask Dr. Smith.", "He knows."]
    """
    cleaned = normalize_whitespace(text)
    if not cleaned:
        return []

    words = cleaned.split(" ")
    sentences: List[str] = []
    current: List[str] = []

    for i, word in enumerate(words):
        current.append(word)

        # Last word: always ends the sentence
        if i == len(words) - 1:
            if current:
                sentences.append(" ".join(current))
            current = []
            continue

        # Check if this word ends a sentence
        if word not in _ABBREVIATIONS and _ends_with_terminator(word):
            if _next_word_starts_sentence(words[i + 1]):
                sentences.append(" ".join(current))
                current = []

    # If anything is left (shouldn't happen due to last-word handling, but safe)
    if current:
        sentences.append(" ".join(current))

    return sentences

def to_camel_case(name: str, upper_first: bool = False) -> str:
    """
    Convert an identifier written in any naming convention to camelCase, or to
    PascalCase when `upper_first` is True.

    The words come from split_identifier(). The first word stays lowercase
    (capitalized when upper_first=True); every following word is capitalized
    (first character upper case, the rest lower case). Words are concatenated
    without separators. Returns "" when there are no words.

    Examples:
        to_camel_case("user_account_id") == "userAccountId"
        to_camel_case("user_account_id", upper_first=True) == "UserAccountId"
    """
    words = split_identifier(name)
    if not words:
        return ""

    if upper_first:
        first = words[0].capitalize()
    else:
        first = words[0].lower()

    rest = "".join(w.capitalize() for w in words[1:])
    return first + rest

def normalize_whitespace(text: str) -> str:
    """
    Collapse every run of whitespace in `text` into a single ASCII space and
    strip leading and trailing whitespace.

    "Whitespace" means any character for which str.isspace() is true: spaces, tabs,
    newlines, non-breaking spaces (U+00A0), em spaces and so on. This is the first
    cleanup step applied to titles, excerpts and user-submitted copy.

    Examples:
        normalize_whitespace("  Hello \\t\\n world  ") == "Hello world"
        normalize_whitespace("") == ""
    """
    # Split on any whitespace (handles all str.isspace() characters) and rejoin with single spaces
    return " ".join(text.split())

import unicodedata
from typing import Optional

from .tokenize_words import tokenize_words


def slugify(text: str, max_length: Optional[int] = None) -> str:
    """
    Build a URL slug from a title.

    The text is split into words with tokenize_words(). Each word is reduced to
    ASCII by stripping diacritics (Unicode NFKD decomposition, then dropping
    non-ASCII characters), after which any remaining character other than a-z and
    0-9 is removed; words that end up empty are discarded. The remaining words are
    joined with "-", so the slug only contains a-z, 0-9 and "-".

    If `max_length` is given, the slug is shortened to at most max_length
    characters and never ends with "-". Raises ValueError if max_length is given
    and is < 1.

    Examples:
        slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world"
        slugify("Crème Brûlée Recipes") == "creme-brulee-recipes"
        slugify("50% off: Summer Sale") == "50-off-summer-sale"
    """
    if max_length is not None and max_length < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_length must be >= 1")

    def normalize_word(word: str) -> str:
        # NFKD decomposition to separate base characters from diacritics
        normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", word)
        # Keep only ASCII characters
        ascii_only = "".join(c for c in normalized if ord(c) < 128)
        # Keep only a-z and 0-9
        return "".join(c for c in ascii_only if c.isalnum())

    # Tokenize and normalize words
    tokens = tokenize_words(text)
    normalized_words = []
    for token in tokens:
        normalized = normalize_word(token)
        if normalized:
            normalized_words.append(normalized)

    # Join with hyphens

from .normalize_whitespace import normalize_whitespace


def truncate_text(text: str, max_chars: int, ellipsis: str = "...") -> str:
    """
    Shorten `text` for previews and teasers without cutting words in half.

    The text is first cleaned with normalize_whitespace(). If the cleaned text has
    at most `max_chars` characters it is returned as is. Otherwise the result is the
    longest run of whole leading words (joined by single spaces) such that the
    words plus `ellipsis` fit in max_chars characters, followed by `ellipsis`. If
    not even the first word fits, the first word is hard-cut so that the result is
    exactly max_chars characters long. Raises ValueError if
    max_chars <= len(ellipsis).

    Examples:
        truncate_text("The quick brown fox jumps", 15) == "The quick..."
        truncate_text("Short text", 50) == "Short text"

    if max_chars <= len(ellipsis):
        raise ValueError("max_chars must be greater than the length of the ellipsis")

    normalized = normalize_whitespace(text)
    if len(normalized) <= max_chars:
        return normalized

    words = normalized.split()
    if not words:
        return ""

    # Find the longest run of words that fits with the ellipsis
    best_run = ""
    for i in range(1, len(words) + 1):
        current_run = " ".join(words[:i])
        if len(current_run) + len(ellipsis) <= max_chars:
            best_run = current_run
        else:
            break

    if best_run:
        # Strip trailing punctuation to avoid double punctuation with ellipsis
        return best_run.rstrip(",.!?;:") + ellipsis

    # If not even the first word fits with the ellipsis, hard-cut it
    # so that the total length including ellipsis is exactly max_chars
    return words[0][:max_chars - len(ellipsis)] + ellipsis

For `justify_text`, I need to handle the space distribution: extra spaces go to the leftmost gaps first. If a line is a single word or the last line, it's left-aligned. Over-long words remain as-is.", "action": {"tool": "write_file", "args": {"path": "src/textkit/wrap_text.py", "content": "from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union
from .normalize_whitespace import normalize_whitespace


def wrap_text(text: str, width: int) -> List[str]:
    """
    Greedy word-wrap `text` into lines of at most `width` characters (used for
    plain-text emails).

    The text is cleaned with normalize_whitespace() and split into words on spaces.
    Words are added to the current line, separated by single spaces, as long as the
    line stays within `width`; otherwise a new line is started with that word. Lines
    have no leading or trailing spaces. Empty or whitespace-only text gives [].
    Raises ValueError if width < 1.

    Example:
        wrap_text("the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", 10)
            == ["the quick", "brown fox", "jumps over", "the lazy", "dog"]
    """
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError("width must be at least 1")

    cleaned = normalize_whitespace(text)
    if not cleaned:
        return []

    words = cleaned.split()
    lines = []
    current_line = []
    current_length = 0

    for word in words:
        # length of current line if we add this word (including space if not first word)
        added_length = len(word) + (1 if current_line else 0)
        if current_length + added_length <= width or not current_line:
            current_line.append(word)
            current_length += added_length
        else:
            lines.append(" ".join(current_line))

from textkit.split_identifier import split_identifier

_ACRONYMS = frozenset({"api", "id", "url", "html", "http", "json", "sql", "uuid"})


def humanize_identifier(name: str) -> str:
    words = split_identifier(name)
    if len(words) > 1 and words[-1] == "id":
        words = words[:-1]
    out = []
    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        if word in _ACRONYMS:
            out.append(word.upper())

        else:

from collections import Counter
from typing import Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple

from textkit.tokenize_words import tokenize_words


def top_words(text: str, k: int, stopwords: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
    """
    Return the `k` most frequent words of `text` as (word, count) pairs, most
    frequent first. Feeds the "top terms" panel of the article analytics page.

    Words come from tokenize_words(). Words listed in `stopwords` (compared
    case-insensitively) are ignored, and so are tokens made only of digits. If fewer
    than k distinct words remain, all of them are returned. Raises ValueError if
    k < 0.

    Examples:
        top_words("b a b c b a", 2) == [("b", 3), ("a", 2)]
        top_words("Data, data and more DATA", 1, stopwords=["and"]) == [("data", 3)]
    """
    if k < 0:
        raise ValueError("k must be non-negative")

    words = tokenize_words(text)
    
    stop_set = set()
    if stopwords is not None:
        stop_set = {s.lower() for s in stopwords}

    filtered_words = [
        w for w in words
        if w not in stop_set and not w.isdigit()
    ]

    counts = Counter(filtered_words)
    
    # Sort by count descending, then by word ascending for ties
    sorted_words = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))
    
    return sorted_words[:k]
"}}, "messages": []}

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union
from .wrap_text import wrap_text


def justify_text(text: str, width: int) -> List[str]:
    """
    Fully justify `text` to a fixed column width for plain-text newsletters.

    Lines are produced with wrap_text(text, width). Every line except the last one
    is then stretched to exactly `width` characters by widening the gaps between
    its words: the extra spaces are spread as evenly as possible, and when they do
    not divide evenly the leftmost gaps get one more space than the others.
    The last line is left-aligned (single spaces between words), and so is any
    line that holds a single word. A line already longer than width (a single
    over-long word) is left as it is. Raises ValueError if width < 1.

    Example:
        justify_text("This is an example of text justification.", 16)[:2]
            == ["This    is    an", "example  of text"]
    """
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError("width must be at least 1")

    lines = wrap_text(text, width)
    if not lines:
        return []

    result = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        words = line.split()
        # Handle single-word lines or over-long words
        if len(words) <= 1:
            # Over-long words (len > width) are returned unpadded per spec
            if len(line) > width:
                result.append(line)
            else:
                result.append(line.ljust(width))
            continue

        # Handle last line: left-aligned, padded on right
        if i == len(lines) - 1:
            result.append(line.ljust(width))
            continue

        # Full justification for other lines
        total_word_len = sum(len(w) for w in words)
        spaces_to_add = width - total_word_len
        num_gaps = len(words) - 1
        
        # Calculate distribution of spaces
        space_per_gap = spaces_to_add // num_gaps
        extra_spaces = spaces_to_add % num_gaps

        justified_line = ""
        for j in range(num_gaps):
            justified_line += words[j]
            # Add base spaces + 1 extra if within the remainder
            current_gap = space_per_gap + (1 if j < extra_spaces else 0)
            justified_line += " " * current_gap
        
        justified_line += words[-1]
        result.append(justified_line)

    return result
"}}, "messages": []}

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union


def count_syllables(word: str) -> int:
    """
    Estimate the number of syllables in an English word (heuristic used by the
    readability score).

    The word is lowercased and every character other than a-z is removed. Then:
      1. Count the groups of consecutive vowels, where vowels are a, e, i, o, u, y.
      2. Silent e: if the word ends in "e" and there is more than one vowel group,
         subtract 1 ("cake" -> 1, while "the" stays 1).
      3. The result is never below 1 for a word that has at least one letter.
    A word with no letters a-z at all returns 0.

    Examples:
        count_syllables("readability") == 5
        count_syllables("cake") == 1
    """
    import re

    # 0. Preprocessing: lowercase and remove non-a-z
    word = re.sub(r'[^a-z]', '', word.lower())
    if not word:
        return 0

    # 1. Count groups of consecutive vowels
    vowels = 'aeiouy'
    vowel_groups = 0
    is_prev_vowel = False
    for char in word:
        is_vowel = char in vowels
        if is_vowel and not is_prev_vowel:
            vowel_groups += 1
        is_prev_vowel = is_vowel

    # 2. Silent e
    if word.endswith('e') and vowel_groups > 1:
        vowel_groups -= 1

    # 3. Result is never below 1 for a word that has at least one letter
    return max(1, vowel_groups)

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union


def edit_distance(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """
    Return the edit distance between `a` and `b`: the minimum number of
    single-character edits needed to turn `a` into `b`.

    Inserting, deleting or substituting one character each cost 1. The comparison
    is case-sensitive, and the distance is symmetric:
    edit_distance(a, b) == edit_distance(b, a). Used by search suggestions for
    typo tolerance.

    Examples:
        edit_distance("kitten", "sitting") == 3
        edit_distance("", "abc") == 3
    """
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    prev = list(range(m + 1))
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        curr = [i] + [0] * m
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            cost = 0 if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] else 1
            curr[j] = min(
                prev[j] + 1,      # delete
                curr[j - 1] + 1,  # insert
                prev[j - 1] + cost,  # substitute
            )
        prev = curr
    return prev[m]

import re
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple

_HEADING = re.compile(r" {0,3}(#{1,6})(?:[ \t]+(.*?))?[ \t]*")
_FENCE = re.compile(r" {0,3}(```|~~~)")
_CLOSING = re.compile(r"(?:^|[ \t]+)#+$")


def extract_headings(markdown: str) -> List[Tuple[int, str]]:
    headings: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
    fence: Optional[str] = None
    for line in markdown.splitlines():
        fence_match = _FENCE.match(line)
        if fence_match:
            if fence is None:
                fence = fence_match.group(1)
            elif fence == fence_match.group(1):
                fence = None
            continue
        if fence is not None:
            continue
        match = _HEADING.fullmatch(line)
        if match:
            title = _CLOSING.sub("", match.group(2) or "").strip()
            headings.append((len(match.group(1)), title))
    return headings

from textkit.normalize_whitespace import normalize_whitespace


def wrap_text(text: str, width: int) -> List[str]:
    """
    Greedy word-wrap `text` into lines of at most `width` characters (used for
    plain-text emails).

    The text is cleaned with normalize_whitespace() and split into words on spaces.
    Words are added to the current line, separated by single spaces, as long as the
    line stays within `width`; otherwise a new line is started with that word. Lines
    have no leading or trailing spaces. Empty or whitespace-only text gives [].
    Raises ValueError if width < 1.

    Example:
        wrap_text("the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", 10)
            == ["the quick", "brown fox", "jumps over", "the lazy", "dog"]
    """
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"width must be >= 1, got {width}")

    cleaned = normalize_whitespace(text)
    if not cleaned:
        return []

    words = cleaned.split(" ")
    lines: List[str] = []
    current = ""

    for word in words:
        if not current:
            current = word
        elif len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= width:
            current += " " + word
        else:
            lines.append(current)
            current = word

    if current:

def edit_distance(a: str, b: str) -> int:

    Inserting, deleting or substituting one character each cost 1. The comparison

    edit_distance(a, b) == edit_distance(b, a). Used by search suggestions for

    Examples:

        edit_distance("", "abc") == 3
    """
    return _damerau_levenshtein(a, b)


def _damerau_levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """Case-insensitive Damerau-Levenshtein distance (adjacent transposition = 1)."""
    a = a.lower()
    b = b.lower()
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    # (i, j) -> [distance, last row index where a[i] matched]
    last_row = {(i, j): [abs(i - j), 0] for i in range(n + 1) for j in range(m + 1)}
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            # propagate the minimum of the three neighbours into the diagonal cell
            d = min(
                last_row[(i - 1, j - 1)][0],
                last_row[(i - 1, j)][0],
                last_row[(i, j - 1)][0],
            )
            last_row[(i - 1, j - 1)][0] = d
            if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                last_row[(i, j)] = [d, last_row[(i - 1, j - 1)][1]]

                        last_row[(i, j - 1)][0] + 1,

                i > 1
                and j > 1
                and a[i - 2] == b[j - 1]
                and a[i - 1] == b[j - 2]
            ):
                transposed = last_row[(i - 2, j - 2)][0] + 2
                if transposed < last_row[(i, j)][0]:

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union

from textkit.normalize_whitespace import normalize_whitespace


def wrap_text(text: str, width: int) -> List[str]:
    """
    Greedy word-wrap `text` into lines of at most `width` characters (used for
    plain-text emails).

    The text is cleaned with normalize_whitespace() and split into words on spaces.
    Words are added to the current line, separated by single spaces, as long as the
    line stays within `width`; otherwise a new line is started with that word. Lines
    have no leading or trailing spaces. Empty or whitespace-only text gives [].
    Raises ValueError if width < 1.

    Example:
        wrap_text("the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", 10)
            == ["the quick", "brown fox", "jumps over", "the lazy", "dog"]
    """
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"width must be >= 1, got {width}")

    cleaned = normalize_whitespace(text)
    if not cleaned:
        return []

    words = cleaned.split(" ")
    lines: List[str] = []
    current = ""

    for word in words:
        if not current:
            current = word
        elif len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= width:
            current += " " + word
        else:
            lines.append(current)
            current = word

    if current:
        lines.append(current)

    return lines
"},"messages":[]}

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union

from .normalize_whitespace import normalize_whitespace


def truncate_text(text: str, max_chars: int, ellipsis: str = "...") -> str:
    """
    Shorten `text` for previews and teasers without cutting words in half.

    The text is first cleaned with normalize_whitespace(). If the cleaned text has
    at most `max_chars` characters it is returned as is. Otherwise the result is the
    longest run of whole leading words (joined by single spaces) such that the
    words plus `ellipsis` fit in max_chars characters, followed by `ellipsis`. If
    not even the first word fits, the first word is hard-cut so that the result is
    exactly max_chars characters long. Raises ValueError if
    max_chars <= len(ellipsis).

    Examples:
        truncate_text("The quick brown fox jumps", 15) == "The quick..."
        truncate_text("Short text", 50) == "Short text"
    """
    if max_chars <= len(ellipsis):
        raise ValueError("max_chars must be greater than the length of the ellipsis")

    normalized = normalize_whitespace(text)
    if len(normalized) <= max_chars:
        return normalized

    words = normalized.split()
    if not words:
        return ""

    # Find the longest run of words that fits with the ellipsis
    best_run = ""
    for i in range(1, len(words) + 1):
        current_run = " ".join(words[:i])
        if len(current_run) + len(ellipsis) <= max_chars:
            best_run = current_run
        else:
            break

    if best_run:
        # Strip trailing punctuation to avoid double punctuation with ellipsis
        return best_run.rstrip(",.!?;:") + ellipsis

    # If not even the first word fits with the ellipsis, hard-cut it
    # so that the total length including ellipsis is exactly max_chars
    return words[0][:max_chars - len(ellipsis)] + ellipsis

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import Counter
from typing import Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple

from textkit.tokenize_words import tokenize_words


def top_words(text: str, k: int, stopwords: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
    """
    Return the `k` most frequent words of `text` as (word, count) pairs, most
    frequent first. Feeds the "top terms" panel of the article analytics page.

    Words come from tokenize_words(). Words listed in `stopwords` (compared
    case-insensitively) are ignored, and so are tokens made only of digits. If fewer
    than k distinct words remain, all of them are returned. Raises ValueError if
    k < 0.

    Examples:
        top_words("b a b c b a", 2) == [("b", 3), ("a", 2)]
        top_words("Data, data and more DATA", 1, stopwords=["and"]) == [("data", 3)]
    """
    if k < 0:
        raise ValueError("k must be non-negative")

    words = tokenize_words(text)
    
    stop_set = set()
    if stopwords is not None:
        stop_set = {s.lower() for s in stopwords}

    filtered_words = [
        w for w in words
        if w not in stop_set and not w.isdigit()
    ]

    counts = Counter(filtered_words)
    
    # Sort by count descending, then by word ascending for ties
    sorted_words = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))
    
    return sorted_words[:k]

    """
    Return the edit distance between `a` and `b`: the minimum number of
    single-character edits needed to turn `a` into `b`.

    Inserting, deleting or substituting one character each cost 1. The comparison
    is case-sensitive, and the distance is symmetric:
    edit_distance(a, b) == edit_distance(b, a). Used by search suggestions for

    Examples:
        edit_distance("kitten", "sitting") == 3
        edit_distance("", "abc") == 3
    """
    return _damerau_levenshtein(a, b)


def _damerau_levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """Case-insensitive Damerau-Levenshtein distance (adjacent transposition = 1)."""
    a = a.lower()
    b = b.lower()
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    if n == 0:
        return m
    if m == 0:
        return n

    da: dict[str, int] = {}
    prev = list(range(m + 1))
    curr = [0] * (m + 1)

    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        da.clear()
        curr[0] = i
        last_j = 0
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            cost = 0 if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] else 1
            if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                da[b[j - 1]] = j
            else:
                da[b[j - 1]] = 0

                curr[j - 1] + 1,  # insertion

            curr[j] = d
            last_j = j

def edit_distance(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """

    single-character edits needed to turn `a` into `b`.

    Inserting, deleting or substituting one character each cost 1. The comparison
    is case-sensitive, and the distance is symmetric:
    edit_distance(a, b) == edit_distance(b, a). Used by search suggestions for

    Examples:

        edit_distance("", "abc") == 3
    """
    return _damerau_levenshtein(a, b)


def _damerau_levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """Case-insensitive Damerau-Levenshtein distance (adjacent transposition = 1)."""
    a = a.lower()
    b = b.lower()
    n, m = len(a), len(b)

    # d[i][j] = edit distance between a[:i] and b[:j]
    # lm[i][j] = last row index where a[i] matched b[:j]
    d = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    lm = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]

    for j in range(m + 1):
        d[0][j] = j

            d[i][j] = min(

                d[i][j - 1] + 1,      # insertion
                d[i - 1][j - 1] + cost,  # substitution

            if i > 1 and j > 1 and a[i - 2] == b[j - 1] and a[i - 1] == b[j - 2]:
                k = lm[i - 2][j - 1]
                if k:

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union

from textkit.normalize_whitespace import normalize_whitespace
from .normalize_whitespace import normalize_whitespace


def wrap_text(text: str, width: int) -> List[str]:
    """
    Greedy word-wrap `text` into lines of at most `width` characters (used for
    plain-text emails).

    The text is cleaned with normalize_whitespace() and split into words on spaces.
    Words are added to the current line, separated by single spaces, as long as the
    line stays within `width`; otherwise a new line is started with that word. Lines
    have no leading or trailing spaces. Empty or whitespace-only text gives [].
    Raises ValueError if width < 1.

    Example:
        wrap_text("the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", 10)
            == ["the quick", "brown fox", "jumps over", "the lazy", "dog"]
    """
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError("width must be at least 1")

    cleaned = normalize_whitespace(text)
    if not cleaned:
        return []

    words = cleaned.split()
    lines = []
    current_line = []
    current_length = 0

    for word in words:
        # length of current line if we add this word (including space if not first word)
        added_length = len(word) + (1 if current_line else 0)
        if current_length + added_length <= width or not current_line:
            current_line.append(word)
            current_length += added_length
        else:
            lines.append(" ".join(current_line))
            current_line = [word]
            current_length = len(word)

    if current_line:
        lines.append(" ".join(current_line))

    return lines

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List, Sequence, Tuple

from textkit.similarity import similarity


def rank_matches(query: str, candidates: Sequence[str], limit: int = 5, min_score: float = 0.0) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
    """
    Rank `candidates` by how closely they match `query` and return the best ones
    as (candidate, score) pairs, best score first. Used by the tag picker.

    The score of a candidate is similarity(query, candidate). Candidates scoring
    below `min_score` are dropped, then at most `limit` pairs are returned.
    Duplicate candidate strings are only ranked once. `candidates` is not modified.
    Raises ValueError if limit < 0.

    Example:
        rank_matches("python", ["java", "python", "pythons"], limit=2)
            == [("python", 1.0), ("pythons", 0.86)]
    """
    if limit < 0:
        raise ValueError("limit must be >= 0")

    seen: set = set()
    scored: List[Tuple[str, float]] = []
    for cand in candidates:
        if cand in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(cand)
        score = similarity(query, cand)
        if score >= min_score:
            scored.append((cand, score))

    scored.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[1], reverse=True)
    return scored[:limit]

from __future__ import annotations


def edit_distance(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """
    Return the edit distance between `a` and `b`: the minimum number of
    single-character edits needed to turn `a` into `b`.

    Inserting, deleting or substituting one character each cost 1. The comparison
    is case-sensitive, and the distance is symmetric:
    edit_distance(a, b) == edit_distance(b, a). Used by search suggestions for
    typo tolerance.

    Examples:
        edit_distance("kitten", "sitting") == 3
        edit_distance("", "abc") == 3
    """
    return _damerau_levenshtein(a, b)


def _damerau_levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """Case-insensitive Damerau-Levenshtein distance (adjacent transposition = 1)."""
    a = a.lower()
    b = b.lower()
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    if n == 0:
        return m
    if m == 0:
        return n

    da: dict[str, int] = {}
    prev = list(range(m + 1))
    curr = [0] * (m + 1)

    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        da.clear()
        curr[0] = i
        last_j = 0
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            cost = 0 if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] else 1
            if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                da[b[j - 1]] = j
            else:
                da[b[j - 1]] = 0

            d = min(
                prev[j] + 1,      # deletion
                curr[j - 1] + 1,  # insertion
                prev[j - 1] + cost,  # substitution
            )

            k = da.get(a[i - 1], 0)
            if k:
                l = last_j
                if k < l:
                    d = min(d, prev[k - 1] + (j - k - 1) + 1 + (l - k - 1))
            curr[j] = d
            last_j = j
        prev, curr = curr, prev
    return prev[m]

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union


def count_syllables(word: str) -> int:
    """
    Estimate the number of syllables in an English word (heuristic used by the
    readability score).

    The word is lowercased and every character other than a-z is removed. Then:
      1. Count the groups of consecutive vowels, where vowels are a, e, i, o, u, y.
      2. Silent e: if the word ends in "e" and there is more than one vowel group,
         subtract 1 ("cake" -> 1, while "the" stays 1).
      3. The result is never below 1 for a word that has at least one letter.
    A word with no letters a-z at all returns 0.

    Examples:
        count_syllables("readability") == 5
        count_syllables("cake") == 1
    """
    import re

    # 0. Preprocessing: lowercase and remove non-a-z
    word = re.sub(r'[^a-z]', '', word.lower())
    if not word:
        return 0

    # 1. Count groups of consecutive vowels
    vowels = 'aeiouy'
    vowel_groups = 0
    is_prev_vowel = False
    for char in word:
        is_vowel = char in vowels
        if is_vowel and not is_prev_vowel:
            vowel_groups += 1
        is_prev_vowel = is_vowel

    # 2. Silent e
    if word.endswith('e') and vowel_groups > 1:
        vowel_groups -= 1

    # 3. Result is never below 1 for a word that has at least one letter
    return max(1, vowel_groups)

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple, Union
from .wrap_text import wrap_text


def justify_text(text: str, width: int) -> List[str]:
    """
    Fully justify `text` to a fixed column width for plain-text newsletters.

    Lines are produced with wrap_text(text, width). Every line except the last one
    is then stretched to exactly `width` characters by widening the gaps between
    its words: the extra spaces are spread as evenly as possible, and when they do
    not divide evenly the leftmost gaps get one more space than the others.
    The last line is left-aligned (single spaces between words), and so is any
    line that holds a single word. A line already longer than width (a single
    over-long word) is left as it is. Raises ValueError if width < 1.

    Example:
        justify_text("This is an example of text justification.", 16)[:2]
            == ["This    is    an", "example  of text"]
    """
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError("width must be at least 1")

    lines = wrap_text(text, width)
    if not lines:
        return []

    result = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        words = line.split()
        # Handle single-word lines or over-long words
        if len(words) <= 1:
            # Over-long words (len > width) are returned unpadded per spec
            if len(line) > width:
                result.append(line)
            else:
                result.append(line.ljust(width))
            continue

        # Handle last line: left-aligned, padded on right
        if i == len(lines) - 1:
            result.append(line.ljust(width))
            continue

        # Full justification for other lines
        total_word_len = sum(len(w) for w in words)
        spaces_to_add = width - total_word_len
        num_gaps = len(words) - 1
        
        # Calculate distribution of spaces
        space_per_gap = spaces_to_add // num_gaps
        extra_spaces = spaces_to_add % num_gaps

        justified_line = ""
        for j in range(num_gaps):
            justified_line += words[j]
            # Add base spaces + 1 extra if within the remainder
            current_gap = space_per_gap + (1 if j < extra_spaces else 0)
            justified_line += " " * current_gap
        
        justified_line += words[-1]
        result.append(justified_line)

    return result

    Inserting, deleting or substituting one character each cost 1. The comparison

    edit_distance(a, b) == edit_distance(b, a). Used by search suggestions for

    Examples:

        edit_distance("", "abc") == 3
    """
    return _damerau_levenshtein(a, b)


def _damerau_levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """Case-insensitive Damerau-Levenshtein distance (adjacent transposition = 1)."""
    a = a.lower()
    b = b.lower()
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    if n == 0:
        return m
    if m == 0:

    curr = [0] * (m + 1)

            cost = 0 if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] else 1
            if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:

def edit_distance(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """
    Return the edit distance between `a` and `b`: the minimum number of
    single-character edits needed to turn `a` into `b`.

    Inserting, deleting or substituting one character each cost 1. The comparison
    is case-sensitive, and the distance is symmetric:
    edit_distance(a, b) == edit_distance(b, a). Used by search suggestions for
    typo tolerance.

    Examples:
        edit_distance("kitten", "sitting") == 3
        edit_distance("", "abc") == 3
    """
    return _damerau_levenshtein(a, b)


def _damerau_levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """Case-insensitive Damerau-Levenshtein distance (adjacent transposition = 1)."""
    a = a.lower()
    b = b.lower()
    n, m = len(a), len(b)

    # d[i][j] = edit distance between a[:i] and b[:j]
    # lm[i][j] = last row index where a[i] matched b[:j]
    d = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    lm = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]

    for i in range(n + 1):
        d[i][0] = i
    for j in range(m + 1):
        d[0][j] = j

    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            cost = 0 if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] else 1
            d[i][j] = min(
                d[i - 1][j] + 1,      # deletion
                d[i][j - 1] + 1,      # insertion
                d[i - 1][j - 1] + cost,  # substitution
            )
            if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                lm[i][j] = j
            else:
                lm[i][j] = lm[i][j - 1]

            # transposition
            if i > 1 and j > 1 and a[i - 2] == b[j - 1] and a[i - 1] == b[j - 2]:
                k = lm[i - 2][j - 1]
                if k:
                    d[i][j] = min(d[i][j], d[i - 2][k - 1] + (j - k - 1) + 1 + (k - 0))
    return d[n][m]"}}, "messages": []}

def _damerau_levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """Case-insensitive Damerau-Levenshtein distance (adjacent transposition = 1)."""

    if n == 0:

    """Case-insensitive Damerau-Levenshtein distance (adjacent transposition = 1)."""

import re
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple

_HEADING = re.compile(r" {0,3}(#{1,6})(?:[ \t]+(.*?))?[ \t]*")
_FENCE = re.compile(r" {0,3}(```|~~~)")
_CLOSING = re.compile(r"(?:^|[ \t]+)#+$")


def extract_headings(markdown: str) -> List[Tuple[int, str]]:
    headings: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
    fence: Optional[str] = None
    for line in markdown.splitlines():
        fence_match = _FENCE.match(line)
        if fence_match:
            if fence is None:
                fence = fence_match.group(1)
            elif fence == fence_match.group(1):
                fence = None
            continue
        if fence is not None:
            continue
        match = _HEADING.fullmatch(line)
        if match:
            title = _CLOSING.sub("", match.group(2) or "").strip()
            headings.append((len(match.group(1)), title))
    return headings

import re
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple

_HEADING = re.compile(r" {0,3}(#{1,6})(?:[ \t]+(.*?))?[ \t]*")
_FENCE = re.compile(r" {0,3}(```|~~~)")
_CLOSING = re.compile(r"(?:^|[ \t]+)#+$")


def extract_headings(markdown: str) -> List[Tuple[int, str]]:
    headings: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
    fence: Optional[str] = None
    for line in markdown.splitlines():
        fence_match = _FENCE.match(line)
        if fence_match:
            if fence is None:
                fence = fence_match.group(1)
            elif fence == fence_match.group(1):
                fence = None
            continue
        if fence is not None:
            continue
        match = _HEADING.fullmatch(line)
        if match:
            title = _CLOSING.sub("", match.group(2) or "").strip()
            headings.append((len(match.group(1)), title))
    return headings
